name: PROSE Awards
notes: Importer uses the official PROSE Awards winners archive and keeps book-like nonfiction categories relevant to a broad public nonfiction index, including Outstanding Work by a Trade Publisher. It excludes technical, professional, education, reference, journal, and narrow scholarly categories that would otherwise over-weight specialist publishing; finalist PDFs should be imported in a later pass.

categories.name: Book Journalism

categories.coverageNotes: Covers official Book category honorees listed in the U.S. Hillman Prize previous-honorees table. Multiple Book rows in a year are normalized as co-winners.

name: Lionel Gelber Prize
organization: Munk School of Global Affairs & Public Policy / Foreign Policy
notes: One of the world's richest nonfiction prizes (CA$50,000), awarded for the best English-language nonfiction book on international affairs. Co-presented by the Munk School at the University of Toronto and Foreign Policy magazine. Shortlist data available from 2011 onward; earlier years record winners only.

categories.name: International Affairs
categories.sourceLabel: Wikipedia: Lionel Gelber Prize
categories.coverageNotes: Winners from 1990 onward (no entry for 2005). Shortlist data available from 2011 onward; 2015, 2020, and 2021 have winner only.

name: Duff Cooper Prize
notes: One of the oldest continuous nonfiction prizes in the UK, awarded since 1956 for the best work of history, biography, or political science published in English or French. Currently sponsored by Pol Roger champagne (Pol Roger Duff Cooper Prize). Winners only — no shortlist is announced.

categories.name: History, Biography & Political Science
categories.sourceLabel: Wikipedia: Duff Cooper Prize
categories.coverageNotes: Winners from 1956 onward. No shortlist is announced for this prize.

name: FT Business Book of the Year
notes: Annual prize for the best business book of the year, backed by the Financial Times. Sponsor has changed: Goldman Sachs (2005–2013), McKinsey (2014–2021), Schroders (2023–present). Prize is £30,000. One of the most internationally recognized nonfiction awards, covering economics, business, politics, and social science.

categories.name: Business Book of the Year
categories.sourceLabel: Wikipedia: Financial Times Business Book of the Year Award
categories.coverageNotes: Winners and shortlists from 2005 onward. Wikipedia article uses prose bullet lists (not a wikitable); winners marked with {{blue ribbon}} template.

name: British Academy Book Prize
notes: Launched in 2013 to recognize outstanding nonfiction in the humanities and social sciences. Formerly known as the British Academy Book Prize for Global Cultural Understanding and earlier as the Nayef Al-Rodhan Prize.

categories.name: British Academy Book Prize
categories.sourceLabel: British Academy Book Prize past-winners archive
categories.coverageNotes: Currently imports official winner and shortlist rows from 2018 onward. Earlier 2013–2017 archive pages require separate QA because their page structure differs from the modern annual pages.

name: Governor General's Literary Awards
notes: Canada's national literary awards, presented since 1936. This registry entry covers the English-language non-fiction category. Initial importer uses the Wikipedia decade tables as a deterministic secondary source while retaining the official GGBooks archive for later verification.

categories.name: English-language Non-fiction
categories.sourceLabel: Wikipedia: Governor General's Award for English-language non-fiction
categories.coverageNotes: Winners from 1936 onward; finalists as listed from 1980 onward. Several 1940s years list multiple winners, reflecting the era's split academic/creative non-fiction categories; these are normalized as co-winners.
